A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diff3DS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses and result galleries.

before.justification: V1 reports original text-to-3D and image-to-3D experiments, quantitative comparisons, qualitative outputs and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original generation experiments and adds a user study, quantitative efficiency analysis and colored multi-view reconstruction experiments.

M1.justification: The rational-curve representation, perspective projection, depth sorting, SDS objectives, Dynamic Noise Deletion and Time Annealing Schedule are retained. The new attribute-optimization and rasterizer-integration experiments exercise existing capabilities without specifying a revised Diff3DS algorithm.

E1.justification: The original 35-prompt and 25-image evaluations remain. V2 adds colored multi-view reconstruction using toyhorse/toycar from the 3Doodle dataset and hotdog/ship/lego from NeRF synthetic data (Appendix D.8), plus a reconstruction comparison using generated multi-view observations (D.7). These introduce substantially different supervision and output requirements.

E2.justification: 3Doodle, explicitly excluded from evaluation in v1, is evaluated in v2's image-to-3D comparison, user study and multi-view experiments. DiffSketcher and CLIPasso are removed from quantitative Tables 1 and 2, respectively, while remaining qualitative references. V2 also compares original 3Doodle against its variant using the Diff3DS rasterizer.

E3.justification: Main CLIP evaluation changes from four orthogonal views to eight rendered views. V2 adds BLIP-Score for text conditioning and reference-view LPIPS for image conditioning. New protocols include randomized Likert evaluations across 25 tasks with 40 participants, and reconstruction comparisons using 120 synthesized horizontal views. The original training settings remain in Appendix A.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative curve-count efficiency analysis, noise-sampling and initialization-radius sensitivity tests, color/opacity/width optimization tests, controlled rasterizer substitution, multi-view reconstruction comparisons and a stylization demonstration (Appendix D.3-D.9). The existing TAS/DND ablation is retained in D.1 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's participant counts and aggregate user ratings add evaluation-design information and results, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 replace the earlier four-view CLIP results with eight-view results and add BLIP/LPIPS entries; these are not same-setting performance gains. New user ratings are 4.18 for Diff3DS, 2.12 for 3Doodle and 1.78 for NEF (Figure 7). Table 2 favors 3Doodle over Diff3DS on LPIPS, 0.2567 versus 0.2647, while Diff3DS leads CLIP. Appendix D adds efficiency, sensitivity and colored-occlusion findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13 and Appendices B-C retain the projection proof, gradient formulations, closest-distance derivations and isolator-polynomial reasoning. Wording and typesetting changes do not alter their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central claims about differentiable, view-consistent sketch generation from text or a single image remain. V2 refines the second stated contribution and conclusion to explicitly emphasize precise rendering of both black and colored curves and the rasterizer's potential for colored 3D sketches.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries: it discusses evaluation without ground-truth sketches, explains the semantic consequences of incorrect colored occlusions, attributes diminishing curve-count returns to noise deletion, and hypothesizes why width optimization is unstable. It also adds initialization guidance, noise/detail tradeoffs and the limitation of manually choosing the curve budget, while retaining v1's principal limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies the noise-deletion threshold as 0.1; v1 left it unspecified. Appendix D documents study presentation, multi-view data generation and Illustrator-based stylization. Existing optimization settings, hardware, STEP output and project access information are retained or relocated. V1's NEF/PidiNet preprocessing description is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds wire-art positioning and references, including WireRoom, Fabricable 3D Wire Art and Wired Perspectives, alongside VecFusion/NIVEL and BLIP/LPIPS citations. It refines 3Doodle's projection characterization from orthogonal to approximate perspective and drops the PidiNet and text-guided vector-customization references. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, rasterizer explanation, evaluation discussion and conclusion receive localized rewriting. Qualitative comparisons now precede quantitative comparisons, implementation details are consolidated in Appendix A, and the component ablation moves to Appendix D.1. Most methodological prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Tables 1-2, adds Table 3, expands the image-comparison figure and introduces user-study, sensitivity, colored-rasterizer and stylization displays. The document adopts the ICLR layout and relocates several figures. The original supplementary result galleries are retained as Figures 18-21 rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's empirical support: it evaluates the previously missing 3Doodle comparator, tests reconstruction with multi-view inputs, adds human judgments and directly tests the rasterizer through controlled substitution (Sections 6.3-6.4; Appendix D). These additions substantially strengthen evidence for the proposed rendering advantages and clarify practical failure conditions. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the changed view protocol prevents interpreting revised scores as cross-version performance gains.
